findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools, get_people, get_pending_replies, resolve_person, get_person_photos · Private data: get_context_pack, get_events, get_people, update_person, log_food, update_food, log_event, update_event, log_moment, update_moment, create_pending_reply, get_pending_replies, update_pending_reply, resolve_pending_reply, log_interaction, get_memories, get_expenses, resolve_person, get_interactions, get_trackers, reset_tracker, search, get_goals, create_goal, update_goal, create_tracker, log_sleep, get_sleep, get_sleep_summary, update_sleep, create_person, get_birthdays, upload_photo, log_expense, log_transaction, log_income, get_person_photos, get_moments, search_moments, get_timeline, get_today · Public sink: get_people, update_person, log_food, update_food, log_event, update_event, create_pending_reply, log_interaction, reset_tracker, get_birthdays, upload_photo · Destructive: get_trackers, reset_tracker, create_tracker.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
